articles.description: The week, the Windows developer said it would offer buyouts to 60,000 workers as it looks to curb costs.

key_points: On Monday, the Windows developer said it would offer voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 of its workers to cut costs as it pours billions of dollars into artificial intelligence (AI).

Microsoft shares rose by almost 2.9% in after hours trading in New York on Wednesday.

articles.description: The chancellor announced a series of measures which will impact under-25 year-olds from housing to minimum wage.

articles.title: Dharshini David: Healey buys himself some time, but big questions still unanswered
articles.description: The chancellor talked of charting a new course for Britain, but the impact of Iran war has limited his options.
articles.summary: While earnings are rising, forecasters predict that is not compensating for higher prices and taxes John Healey talked of charting a new course for Britain, but this Budget was more about course-correcting than charging down a new path.
key_points: It was abundantly clear that the financial fallout from that conflict in the Middle East has hampered the finances of households and businesses – and the government's ability to help.
While the government targeted those impacted by higher energy and fuel bills, the "breathing space" it aimed to provide was limited; it is a pill that doesn't fully alleviate the pain.
The most telling evidence was that official forecasters predict that while earnings will rise, that is not compensating for higher prices and taxes.

articles.title: Assumptions Beyond the Future Budget 2027
No Sacred Cows: A Playbook for Mid-Year Budget Reallocation
articles.summary: It’s June, the annual budget was confidently approved in November, and now the numbers aren’t adding up.
key_points: An initiative that looked like the obvious growth driver six months ago is underdelivering, while a smaller, underfunded programme is quietly outperforming its target.
The organisationally difficult move is exactly the same.
